--- title: "An Unaligned-Reference Estimand for Preferential Sampling Bias" jupyter: python3 fig-dpi: 300 bibliography: references.bib --- ```{=html} ``` This report defines a **reference counterfactual** for the preferential sampling bias and estimates it. The construction is: hold the field year fixed, and ask what sampling bias that field would have suffered had the array been advected by a *different* year's circulation. Averaging that over every unaligned circulation gives a reference; the aligned circulation's bias minus that reference is the estimand. Nothing is held out for validation and nothing is refit — the name that suggests otherwise is deliberately avoided. It reads the design ensembles produced and described in [Monte-Carlo Sampling Distributions of the Residual-Field Mean](mean_estimation_mc.html), which is the prerequisite: the analysis measure $\mathbb{P}$, the truth $\bar Z_k$, the residual field $\tilde Z_k$, the two analysis boxes, and the per-cell bias $B_k^{(l,d)} = \hat Z^{(l,d)}_k - \bar Z_k$ are all defined and measured there. In brief, $B_k^{(l,d)}$ is the bias incurred when floats advected by velocity year $l$ under deployment replicate $d$ sample the residual OHC field of analysis year $k$; there are $M = 10$ velocity years, $m = 10$ analysis years, and $D = 750$ deployment replicates per velocity year, in each of two boxes. ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"} **Notation.** $\nu$ denotes a *signed measure* — an empirical sampling measure minus the analysis measure $\mathbb{P}$. $\mu$ denotes a *mean* of such signed measures, i.e. a mean footprint; $\mu(\cdot)$ is the map from a velocity field to its mean footprint. Neither letter is used for anything else. $m(\cdot)$ is reserved for the companion report's fitted mean field, the parametric surface subtracted from OHC to give the residual $\tilde Z$. The bare symbols $m$ and $M$ keep their meaning from the companion report throughout: the number of analysis years and of velocity years respectively, here both $10$. ::: **What is new here, and what is not.** The companion report's §7 forms a *gapped* contrast $T_k$ — the aligned cell against the flows at $|l-k| \ge 2$ — and identifies it with preferential sampling under an assumption (P). The construction below differs in three ways. 1. The target is defined **first, as a functional of the realised record**, and the estimator is then shown to be exactly unbiased for it — with no assumption on the velocity fields, the residual fields, or their relationship. This is a real gain in rigour. It is also a smaller gain than it first appears, because identifying that target *with the preferential sampling bias* is a separate step that does carry an assumption; @sec-ident derives exactly what that assumption is, what it costs when it fails, and how large the failure can be here. 2. The reference uses **every** unaligned flow, $l \ne k$, not a gapped subset. The gap becomes a sensitivity analysis rather than part of the definition. 3. The variance is exact rather than approximated by an across-year spread, including for the pooled estimate, and the full covariance across analysis years is available — which is what makes the drift statement in @sec-drift possible at all. The point estimates are not new. The two estimands differ by the known factor $\tfrac{M-1}{M}$ (@sec-relation), so this report *reframes and re-errors* quantities the companion already reported; it does not overturn them. The companion's hypothesis test is treated separately in [A Permutation Test for Preferential Sampling](permutation_test.html). # The estimand ## Setup The velocity fields $\tilde V_1,\dots,\tilde V_M$ and residual fields $\tilde Z_1,\dots,\tilde Z_M$ are **fixed**: they are realised reanalysis output, and no distribution is placed over them. All randomness enters through the deployment draws $\omega_{l,d} \overset{iid}{\sim} \mathcal{D}$, and every expectation and variance in this section and the next two is with respect to $\mathcal{D}$ alone, conditional on the realised fields. For a design $X = \{x_1,\dots,x_n\} \subset \mathcal{X}$ write $$\nu_X \;:=\; \hat{\mathbb{P}}_X - \mathbb{P}, \qquad \hat{\mathbb{P}}_X \;=\; \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \delta_{x_i},$$ a signed measure of total mass zero on $\mathcal{X}$, whose restriction to the analysis partition $\{c_j\}_{j=1}^C$ is the vector $(w_1 - p_1,\dots,w_C - p_C)$. Because $\tilde Z_k$ is constant within cells, the bias is *exactly* the bilinear pairing $$B_k(X) \;=\; \int_{\mathcal{X}} \tilde Z_k \, d\nu_X \;=\; \langle \nu_X, \tilde Z_k\rangle \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^C (w_j - p_j)\,\tilde Z_{k,j},$$ an identity rather than an approximation: $\tilde Z_k$ is a bounded simple function and $\nu_X$ a finite signed measure. Abbreviate $\nu^{(l,d)} := \nu_{X^{(l,d)}}$ and $B_k^{(l,d)} := \langle \nu^{(l,d)}, \tilde Z_k\rangle$. The object the construction is built on is the **mean footprint** of a velocity year, $$\mu^{(l)} \;:=\; \mathbb{E}_{\omega\sim\mathcal{D}}\big[\nu_{\mathcal{G}(\omega,\,\tilde V_l)}\big],$$ the deployment-averaged design deviation induced by flow year $l$. Since $\mathcal{D}$ and $\tilde V_l$ are fixed, $\mu^{(l)}$ is a deterministic zero-mass signed measure; existence is immediate because $w_j \in [0,1]$ and $C < \infty$, so $\nu^{(l,d)}$ is uniformly bounded. ## The reference counterfactual ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} For an analysis year $k$, the **unaligned reference footprint** is $$\bar\mu^{(-k)} \;:=\; \frac{1}{M-1}\sum_{l \ne k} \mu^{(l)},$$ and the **alignment contrast** is $$\Theta_k \;:=\; \big\langle\, \mu^{(k)} - \bar\mu^{(-k)},\;\; \tilde Z_k \,\big\rangle .$$ ::: In words: the excess sampling bias against field year $k$ produced by that year's own circulation, relative to the bias the remaining $M-1$ circulations would have produced against the *same* field. Both terms are deterministic, so $\Theta_k$ is a **fixed quantity attached to the realised record**, in the units of $\tilde Z$ (J m$^{-2}$) — not a parameter of a population of oceans. **Coverage bias cancels identically.** Let $\mu^{\circ}$ be *any* zero-mass signed measure not depending on $l$, and write $\mu^{(l)} = \mu^{\circ} + \delta^{(l)}$. Then $$\Theta_k \;=\; \big\langle (\mu^{\circ} + \delta^{(k)}) - (\mu^{\circ} + \bar\delta^{(-k)}),\; \tilde Z_k\big\rangle \;=\; \big\langle \delta^{(k)} - \bar\delta^{(-k)},\; \tilde Z_k\big\rangle, \qquad \bar\delta^{(-k)} := \frac{1}{M-1}\sum_{l\ne k}\delta^{(l)},$$ so $\mu^{\circ}$ drops out. The cancellation follows from linearity alone and holds for *any* such $\mu^{\circ}$ — a quantity not varying with $l$ cannot survive a difference taken across $l$. The natural reading of $\mu^{\circ}$ is the array's persistent non-uniformity: deployment geography, the time-mean circulation, and bathymetry. The structure responsible is that $\Theta_k$ differences two **designs** against a **single** field. Had the comparison held the design fixed and varied the field, as in $\langle \mu^{(k)}, \tilde Z_k - \tilde Z_{k'}\rangle$, the common footprint would multiply $\tilde Z_k - \tilde Z_{k'} \ne 0$ and would not cancel. Holding the field fixed while varying the circulation is the load-bearing feature, not an incidental choice. The excluded term $\langle \mu^{\circ}, \tilde Z_k\rangle$ is the **coverage bias**. It is typically the larger of the two contributions to the total $\langle \mu^{(k)}, \tilde Z_k\rangle$, and it is excluded deliberately: coverage bias is a deterministic function of position and can be computed and removed given the profile locations and a climatology, or suppressed by inverse-intensity weighting. Preferential bias admits no such correction — it is a covariance between the design and the component of the field that position does not predict, so reweighting by position cannot reach it. The two differ in kind, not merely in magnitude. **Why the reference excludes $k$.** The alternative is to centre on the finite grand mean $\bar\mu := M^{-1}\sum_l \mu^{(l)}$ and target $\langle \mu^{(k)} - \bar\mu, \tilde Z_k\rangle$. That is less convenient because $\sum_l (\mu^{(l)} - \bar\mu) = 0$ forces the reference to depend on year $k$ itself: any excess in $\mu^{(k)}$ is offset by a compensating deficit spread across the remaining years, so a contrast against a strict subset of them acquires a multiplicative distortion and a residual depending on which years were excluded. Removing $k$ from its own reference eliminates the constraint. The two differ by a known factor, $$\big\langle \mu^{(k)} - \bar\mu, \tilde Z_k\big\rangle \;=\; \frac{M-1}{M}\,\Theta_k,$$ {#eq-grand} verified numerically in @tbl-audit. That same zero-sum constraint has a sharper consequence, which is where the next section starts. # Identification: when is $\Theta_k$ the preferential sampling bias? {#sec-ident} Everything above is exact and assumption-free. But $\Theta_k$ is defined as a contrast of mean footprints; calling it *the preferential sampling bias* is a separate claim requiring a separate argument. This section makes the target explicit, derives the exact gap between it and $\Theta_k$, states the assumption that closes the gap, and measures how large the gap can be. ## First, a trap to avoid It is tempting to phrase the required assumption directly on the decomposition above: "the average unaligned flow anomaly carries no alignment with year $k$'s field," i.e. $\langle \bar\delta^{(-k)}, \tilde Z_k\rangle = 0$. If $\mu^{\circ}$ is taken to be the finite grand mean $\bar\mu$, this is **vacuous**. The reason is the zero-sum constraint. With $\delta^{(l)} := \mu^{(l)} - \bar\mu$ we have $\sum_{l=1}^M \delta^{(l)} = 0$ identically, hence $\sum_{l\ne k}\delta^{(l)} = -\delta^{(k)}$ and $$\bar\delta^{(-k)} \;=\; -\,\frac{\delta^{(k)}}{M-1} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \big\langle \bar\delta^{(-k)}, \tilde Z_k\big\rangle \;=\; -\,\frac{1}{M-1}\big\langle \delta^{(k)}, \tilde Z_k\big\rangle \;\overset{\text{@eq-grand}}{=}\; -\,\frac{1}{M-1}\cdot\frac{M-1}{M}\,\Theta_k \;=\; -\,\frac{\Theta_k}{M}.$$ So with a finite reference, "the average unaligned anomaly carries no alignment" is *algebraically equivalent to $\Theta_k = 0$*. It is the null hypothesis, not an identifying condition, and assuming it would assume the answer away. The cancellation argument of the previous section is untouched — it needs only that $\mu^{\circ}$ not depend on $l$ — but the identification cannot be phrased against a finite average. It needs a **population** reference, which is what the rest of this section builds. ## The decoupling counterfactual Let $\mu(\cdot)$ denote the map taking a velocity field to its mean footprint, so $\mu^{(l)} = \mu(\tilde V_l)$, and let $\mathcal{V}$ be the population law of annual circulations of which $\tilde V_1,\dots,\tilde V_M$ are realisations. Define the **population mean footprint** $$\mu^{\star} \;:=\; \mathbb{E}_{V \sim \mathcal{V}}\big[\mu(V)\big].$$ Now the counterfactual. Suppose the array were advected by a circulation $V^{\perp} \sim \mathcal{V}$ drawn *independently* of $\tilde Z_k$. Its expected footprint is $\mathbb{E}[\mu(V^{\perp}) \mid \tilde Z_k] = \mathbb{E}_{V\sim\mathcal{V}}[\mu(V)] = \mu^{\star}$, the conditioning dropping out precisely by independence. Two features matter: $\mu^\star$ is a single fixed measure, and it **does not depend on $k$**. ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} The **preferential sampling bias** of analysis year $k$ is $$\Pi_k \;:=\; \big\langle\, \mu^{(k)} - \mu^{\star},\;\; \tilde Z_k \,\big\rangle .$$ ::: This is the design-based image of @diggle2010's condition. $\Pi_k$ is nonzero exactly when year $k$'s own footprint departs from the typical footprint *in the direction of* year $k$'s field, which is what it means for the sampling process and the field to fail to factor. Averaging over the population of years, $\mathbb{E}[\Pi] = \mathbb{E}\big[\langle \mu(V) - \mathbb{E}\mu(V), \tilde Z\rangle\big]$ is a covariance between footprint and field, zero under $[S,X] = [S][X]$ and nonzero otherwise. $\Pi_k$ is its single-realisation version. ## The bridge identity Both estimands share the term $\langle \mu^{(k)}, \tilde Z_k\rangle$ and differ only in what they subtract. Four steps, each an identity. **Step 1.** By definition of $\Theta_k$ and linearity of the pairing in its first argument, $$\Theta_k \;=\; \big\langle \mu^{(k)}, \tilde Z_k\big\rangle \;-\; \big\langle \bar\mu^{(-k)}, \tilde Z_k\big\rangle .$$ **Step 2.** By definition of $\Pi_k$, likewise, $$\Pi_k \;=\; \big\langle \mu^{(k)}, \tilde Z_k\big\rangle \;-\; \big\langle \mu^{\star}, \tilde Z_k\big\rangle .$$ **Step 3.** Subtract; the shared term cancels. $$\Theta_k - \Pi_k \;=\; \big\langle \mu^{\star}, \tilde Z_k\big\rangle - \big\langle \bar\mu^{(-k)}, \tilde Z_k\big\rangle \;=\; -\,\big\langle \bar\mu^{(-k)} - \mu^{\star},\; \tilde Z_k \big\rangle .$$ **Step 4.** Redefine the anomaly against the *population* mean, $\delta^{(l)} := \mu^{(l)} - \mu^{\star}$. Since $\mu^\star$ does not depend on $l$, averaging over $l \ne k$ gives $\bar\mu^{(-k)} - \mu^{\star} = (M-1)^{-1}\sum_{l\ne k}(\mu^{(l)} - \mu^{\star}) = \bar\delta^{(-k)}$. Therefore $$\Theta_k \;=\; \Pi_k \;-\; \big\langle \bar\delta^{(-k)},\; \tilde Z_k \big\rangle .$$ {#eq-bridge} @eq-bridge is exact and holds with no assumption whatever. Note what has changed relative to the trap: with $\mu^{\star}$ a population expectation rather than the average of the $M$ realised years, $\sum_l \delta^{(l)} \ne 0$ in general, so the zero-sum constraint that made the condition vacuous is gone. It is convenient to write the whole thing as a matrix of alignments. Put $$c_{lk} \;:=\; \big\langle \delta^{(l)}, \tilde Z_k\big\rangle,$$ the alignment of flow year $l$'s footprint anomaly with field year $k$'s residual field. Then $\Pi_k = c_{kk}$ is the diagonal, and @eq-bridge reads $$\Theta_k \;=\; c_{kk} \;-\; \frac{1}{M-1}\sum_{l \ne k} c_{lk} \;=\; \underbrace{\text{(diagonal)}}_{\Pi_k} \;-\; \underbrace{\text{(off-diagonal mean of column }k)}_{\text{the gap}} .$$ {#eq-cmatrix} ::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"} **Assumption (P$'$).** $\displaystyle \frac{1}{M-1}\sum_{l\ne k} c_{lk} = \big\langle \bar\delta^{(-k)}, \tilde Z_k\big\rangle = 0$. Under (P$'$), @eq-bridge gives $\Theta_k = \Pi_k$ exactly, and $\widehat\Theta_k$ — unbiased for $\Theta_k$ with no assumption — is unbiased for the preferential sampling bias. ::: (P$'$) is weaker than the companion report's (P), which asks $c_{lk} = 0$ for every $l$ in the comparison set. Only the *average* over the $M-1$ reference flows need vanish; individual flows may align with $\tilde Z_k$ provided they cancel. It is also the exact and complete condition: @eq-bridge shows nothing else is needed and nothing less will do. ## How (P$'$) fails, part 1: systematic dependence $c_{lk} \ne 0$ on average whenever $\tilde V_l$ and $\tilde Z_k$ are genuinely dependent — ocean memory. Gyre state and the North Atlantic Oscillation persist over several years, so the circulation of year $k \pm 1$ retains information about year $k$'s field. This is a *bias* in the identification, it does not shrink with $D$, and it is what @sec-contamination measures empirically. ## How (P$'$) fails, part 2: the reference is finite Even with $\tilde V_l$ statistically independent of $\tilde Z_k$ for every $l \ne k$, the gap in @eq-cmatrix is a mean of $M-1 = 9$ terms that are individually mean-zero, not zero. Writing $s_k^2 := \operatorname{Var}_{V\sim\mathcal{V}}\big(\langle \mu(V) - \mu^\star, \tilde Z_k\rangle\big)$ for the population spread of the alignment across circulations, independence across $l$ gives $$\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{1}{M-1}\sum_{l\ne k} c_{lk}\right] = 0, \qquad \operatorname{sd}\left(\frac{1}{M-1}\sum_{l\ne k} c_{lk}\right) = \frac{s_k}{\sqrt{M-1}} .$$ {#eq-reffloor} So $\Theta_k$ is an unbiased-but-noisy stand-in for $\Pi_k$, with a **floor of $s_k/\sqrt{M-1}$ that no amount of deployment replication removes.** Doubling $D$ shrinks the standard error of $\widehat\Theta_k$ as an estimator of $\Theta_k$; it does nothing at all to @eq-reffloor. Two things must be said plainly about the status of @eq-reffloor. First, it is a **superpopulation** statement: it requires the $M$ realised circulations to be a sample from $\mathcal{V}$, which is an exchangeability-flavoured assumption of exactly the kind the design-based framing was built to avoid. Conditional on the realised record — this report's stance everywhere else — $\Theta_k - \Pi_k$ is a fixed unknown number, not a variance. Second, $\mu^\star$ is **not identifiable from these data**: within a column, $\langle \mu^\star, \tilde Z_k\rangle$ and the reference $\bar\mu^{(-k)}$ are confounded, and any attempt to estimate the level of the gap reimposes the zero-sum constraint and returns the vacuity of the trap. What @eq-reffloor supplies is a *scale*, not a correction. $s_k$ is estimable: it is the spread of $\bar G_{kl}$ across the $M-1$ unaligned flows, net of each cell's own Monte-Carlo error, which the companion report reports as the "implied between-flow sd". ::: {#tbl-refnoise .cell execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

"mean corr across years" is the mean pairwise correlation, over the $\binom{m}{2} = 45$ pairs of analysis years, of the within-row deviations that define $s_k$; near zero means each year's reference misses independently. The remaining columns repeat the pooled level and the GLS drift of @sec-drift with the floor added to the covariance as an independent diagonal contribution. {#tbl-refpool} **The correlation is essentially zero** — $-0.08$ in both boxes, with $19$ of $45$ pairs positive and a scatter ($\mathrm{sd} \approx 0.44$) matching what eight shared points give under independence. So there is no detectable flow-year main effect: each analysis year's reference misses $\mu^\star$ in its own direction, and the floor pools down at $\sqrt{m}$ like ordinary noise. Pooled, it adds $0.0026$ GJ/m$^2$ to Box B and $0.0006$ to Box A, and the pooled $t$ falls from $-16.0$ to $-13.4$ and from $+2.8$ to $+2.4$. Both conclusions survive. ## What $\Theta_k$ measures when (P$'$) fails @eq-cmatrix holds regardless, so $\Theta_k$ always measures **exactly one thing, assumption-free**: how much more year $k$'s own circulation aligns with year $k$'s field than the other $M-1$ circulations of this record do. That statement never needs (P$'$). What (P$'$) buys is the upgrade from "than the other nine circulations do" to "than an independent circulation would." Three consequences follow. **1. $\Theta_k$ is a high-pass filter on the coupling, with the record length as the cutoff.** Suppose the flow–field coupling persists over several years — a multi-year gyre regime in which floats trap in warm anomalies. Then $c_{lk}$ is nonzero and of the same sign for $l$, $k$ within the regime, the reference cancels part of the diagonal, and $|\Theta_k| < |\Pi_k|$. Push to the limit in which the coupling is common to all $M$ years, so $c_{lk} \equiv \gamma$ for every $l$ and $k$: then $\Theta_k = \gamma - \gamma = 0$ while $\Pi_k = \gamma \neq 0$. **A perfectly persistent preferential bias is invisible to this construction.** That limit is nonetheless coherent rather than a defect. If every circulation's footprint anomaly aligns identically with every field, the alignment is predictable from position and a climatology, which is the definition of coverage bias — and coverage bias is removable by reweighting, which is why the construction excludes it. What the filter does is reclassify perfectly persistent coupling as coverage rather than preferential, consistently with how the two were separated in the first place. The genuinely awkward case is neither limit but the middle: coupling on a decadal timescale in a decade-long record, which is partly removed and partly retained, with no way to say which part. North Atlantic gyre and NAO timescales put the Box B analysis squarely in that middle. **2. Whether the bias is attenuated or inflated is an assumption about the sign of the coupling.** From @eq-cmatrix, if the off-diagonal $c_{lk}$ carry the same sign as $c_{kk}$ then $|\Theta_k| < |\Pi_k|$ — the familiar attenuation argument, under which $\Theta_k$ is conservative. If they carry the opposite sign then $|\Theta_k| > |\Pi_k|$ and $\Theta_k$ **overstates** the preferential bias. Nothing in the construction forces the first case. @sec-contamination finds the measured direction to be the second, weakly and insignificantly, so "conservative" is not available here as a free guarantee. **3. The drift is better protected than the level.** Take the separable contamination model $c_{lk} = \rho_{|l-k|}\,\Pi_k$ with $\rho_0 = 1$, under which memory scales each column's alignment by its lag. Then @eq-cmatrix gives $$\Theta_k \;=\; \kappa_k \Pi_k, \qquad \kappa_k \;=\; 1 - \frac{1}{M-1}\sum_{l\ne k}\rho_{|l-k|},$$ a purely multiplicative attenuation, with $\kappa_k \in (0,1]$ whenever $\rho \ge 0$. Two things follow. If memory is non-negative, the estimated drift is a **lower bound** on the true drift and its sign and significance are preserved. And $\kappa_k$ varies with $k$ only through edge effects — the first and last analysis years have all their reference flows on one side, so their $\bar\rho_k$ is smaller and they are attenuated *less* than interior years. That dependence is symmetric about the centre of the record, hence quadratic in $k$ and very nearly orthogonal to a linear trend. **Contamination of this form distorts the shape of the $\Theta_k$ series but does not manufacture a drift.** # The estimator Let $\bar G_{kl} := D^{-1}\sum_{d=1}^D B_k^{(l,d)}$ be the cell mean of the simulation array — the heatmap of the companion report, read one row at a time. ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} $$\widehat\Theta_k \;:=\; \bar G_{kk} \;-\; \frac{1}{M-1}\sum_{l \ne k} \bar G_{kl}.$$ ::: **Exact unbiasedness.** $\mathbb{E}[\widehat\Theta_k] = \Theta_k$ for every $k$. Each $\nu^{(l,d)}$ is bounded and $C < \infty$, so $B_k^{(l,d)}$ is integrable and expectation commutes with the finite sums. By linearity of the pairing in its first argument, and because the $\omega_{l,d}$ are identically distributed across $d$, $$\mathbb{E}\big[\bar G_{kl}\big] \;=\; \frac1D \sum_d \big\langle \mathbb{E}[\nu^{(l,d)}], \tilde Z_k\big\rangle \;=\; \big\langle \mu^{(l)}, \tilde Z_k\big\rangle,$$ and applying linearity once more to the definition gives $\Theta_k$. The proof uses only linearity of the pairing, boundedness, and identical distribution of deployment draws *within* a cell. It does **not** require the designs to be identically distributed across velocity years, the residual fields to be exchangeable, or any distributional form for $B$. Those are what it takes to attach a $p$-value, not to estimate $\Theta_k$. Estimation and inference are therefore separable, which matters here because the companion permutation-test report finds two of the four randomisation assumptions rejected by the data: $\widehat\Theta_k$ can be reported with a standard error even where the randomisation hypothesis is in doubt. # Variance Write $\sigma^2_{kl} := \operatorname{Var}_{\omega\sim\mathcal{D}}\big(\langle \nu_{\mathcal{G}(\omega,\tilde V_l)}, \tilde Z_k\rangle\big)$, the deployment variance of the single-design bias in cell $(k,l)$, again finite by boundedness. If the deployment draws are mutually independent across all pairs $(l,d)$ — which this OSSE satisfies, since every velocity year is seeded from its own draw and no common random numbers are used — the cell means $\{\bar G_{kl}\}_l$ are independent and $$\operatorname{Var}\big(\widehat\Theta_k\big) \;=\; \frac1D\left[\sigma^2_{kk} + \frac{1}{(M-1)^2}\sum_{l\ne k}\sigma^2_{kl}\right]. $$ {#eq-var} This is the variance of $\widehat\Theta_k$ **about $\Theta_k$**, over deployment draws with the fields held fixed. It is not the uncertainty about $\Pi_k$, which carries @eq-reffloor in addition. $\sigma^2_{kl}$ is estimated by the within-cell sample variance of $\{B_k^{(l,d)}\}_{d}$, which requires no model. It is worth noting what it is *not*: for $n$ independent draws from $\mathbb{P}$ one would have $\sigma^2_{kl} = \operatorname{Var}_\mathbb{P}(\tilde Z_k)\,\mathbb{E}[1/n]$, but advected floats are strongly clustered along trajectories, so consecutive profiles are near-replicates and the effective sample size is far below $n$. The empirical within-cell variance captures this automatically; the companion report measures the float-clustered design effect at $\approx 1.8$. ## The homoscedastic reduction should not be used If $\sigma^2_{kl} \equiv \sigma^2_k$ for all $l$, @eq-var collapses to $\sigma_k^2 D^{-1}(1 + (M-1)^{-1})$. Its variance does *not* factorise, because $\widehat\Theta_k$ and $\widehat\Theta_{k'}$ are built from the same simulations. A worst-case bound $\max_k \operatorname{Var}(\widehat\Theta_k)$ is available but is very loose — here it overstates the standard error by $3.4\times$ (Box B) and $3.8\times$ (Box A). The exact variance is available in closed form and no resampling is needed. Let $c_{kl}^{\,\mathrm{w}} = \mathbb{1}\{k = l\} - \mathbb{1}\{k \ne l\}/(M-1)$ be the contrast weights, and define the per-draw unit statistic $$U^{(l,d)} \;:=\; \frac1m \sum_k c_{kl}^{\,\mathrm{w}}\, B_k^{(l,d)}, \qquad\text{so that}\qquad \widehat{\bar\Theta} \;=\; \sum_l \frac{1}{D_l}\sum_d U^{(l,d)} .$$ The $U^{(l,d)}$ are independent across $(l,d)$ — every dependence among the $\widehat\Theta_k$ enters through their sharing a *draw*, which the reindexing collects into a single scalar — so $$\operatorname{Var}\big(\widehat{\bar\Theta}\big) \;=\; \sum_l \frac{\operatorname{Var}_d\big(U^{(l,\cdot)}\big)}{D_l} \;=\; \frac{\mathbf{1}^\top \Sigma\, \mathbf{1}}{m^2},$$ with $\Sigma$ the exact covariance matrix of $\{\widehat\Theta_k\}$, assembled the same way. Both routes are computed and agreed in @tbl-audit. The same $\Sigma$ is what @sec-drift needs. Empirically the off-diagonal correlations of $\Sigma$ are tiny — mean $+0.006$, range $-0.03$ to $+0.04$ in both boxes — so pooling gains almost the full $\sqrt{m}$. The cancellation is a property of the construction, and this table is the check that it happened. # Drift, not level {#sec-drift} A preferential offset constant in time affects the estimated mean state but **cancels in anomalies and trends**, which are the quantities used in ocean-heat-uptake and Earth-energy-imbalance assessments. A *time-varying* offset does not. Since the real Argo array roughly tripled between 2004 and 2007, standardised parking depths, changed float models, and expanded to high latitudes, any accompanying change in trapping propensity appears as a spurious heat flux. Estimating $\Theta_k$ separately by year is therefore the more informative use of the construction, and the exact covariance $\Sigma$ makes the drift a well-posed generalized-least-squares problem rather than an ordinary regression on correlated points. Writing $b$ for the GLS slope of $\{\widehat\Theta_k\}$ on year, the implied flux is $10b / (3.1536\times10^8)$ W m$^{-2}$ per decade, the denominator being seconds per decade. **The two boxes separate on exactly this axis**, and in the opposite direction to the levels. - **Box B** has a large level and **no drift**: $b = -0.0001 \pm 0.0013$ GJ/m$^2$/yr, $t = -0.07$, i.e. $-0.003$ W m$^{-2}$ per decade. Adding the reference floor of @eq-reffloor to the covariance (@tbl-refpool) leaves both readings intact: Box A's drift falls to $t = +3.5$ and $+0.052$ W m$^{-2}$ per decade, Box B stays null. Box B's drift *point* estimate is not stable under the reweighting ($-0.003$ against $-0.065$ W m$^{-2}$ per decade), which is itself a symptom of there being no drift for the weights to latch onto. Read carefully, this is the more consequential of the two findings, and it inverts the naive reading of @tbl-theta: the box whose pooled contrast looks like a null control is the one whose contrast is *moving*. Three qualifications belong immediately with it, and are not optional. 1. **The drift is descriptive of these ten years.** It is a least-squares summary of ten correlated numbers attached to a realised record, not an inference to a population of years. The standard error is the Monte Carlo error of the ten $\widehat\Theta_k$, optionally widened by the reference floor; neither includes the variability of the ocean state that generated them. There is one realisation of each year. 2. **A ten-year window cannot separate trend from low-frequency variability.** Gyre state and the North Atlantic Oscillation have decadal timescales, so a monotone $\Theta_k$ over 2010--2019 is equally consistent with one phase of an oscillation. The one reassurance available is structural: by @sec-ident's third point, lag-based contamination distorts the series symmetrically about the record centre and so does not manufacture a linear trend. 3. **The mechanism here is not the mechanism of concern.** The real-Argo drift threat is a *changing array* — more floats, different parking, new regions. This OSSE holds the deployment law fixed by construction and varies only the flow, so what it measures is drift in the flow--field coupling, which is a different thing. The OSSE demonstrates that the quantity is estimable and moves; it does not estimate the historical Argo drift. # Relation to the gapped contrast {#sec-relation} The companion report's statistic is $T_k = \bar G_{kk} - |\mathcal{C}_k|^{-1}\sum_{l\in\mathcal{C}_k} \bar G_{kl}$ with $\mathcal{C}_k = \{l : |l-k| \ge 2\}$, and its per-year table is centred on the *grand* column mean. Two comparisons matter. **The grand-mean version is $\Theta_k$ up to a known factor.** By @eq-grand, centring on $\bar\mu$ rather than $\bar\mu^{(-k)}$ gives exactly $\tfrac{M-1}{M}\Theta_k = 0.9\,\Theta_k$ here; the pooled $-0.0590$ and $+0.0030$ GJ/m$^2$ of the companion's contrast table are $0.9$ times the $-0.0655$ and $+0.0033$ above, to machine precision (@tbl-audit). **This report changes the framing and the error bars, not the measurement.** That is worth stating plainly, because "an unbiased estimator with no assumptions" could otherwise be read as a claim to have measured something the earlier analysis could not. **The variance advantage over a gapped contrast is real and immaterial.** Under the homoscedastic model a gapped contrast with $c = |\mathcal{C}_k| < M-1$ has variance $\sigma_k^2 D^{-1}(1 + c^{-1})$ against $\sigma_k^2 D^{-1}(1 + (M-1)^{-1})$, so the full reference is strictly tighter. With $M = 10$ and $c$ typically $8$, the ratio of standard errors is about $1.006$ — six parts in a thousand. The case for the full reference is that it defines a clean estimand, not that it is more efficient. Any claim resting on the efficiency gain should be dropped. The genuine trade is elsewhere, and @sec-ident locates it: the gap trims the reference flows most likely to violate (P$'$) through memory, at the cost of computing the reference from $c$ rather than $M-1$ flows and so raising the floor of @eq-reffloor from $s_k/\sqrt{M-1}$ to $s_k/\sqrt{c}$. # Is the reference contaminated? {#sec-contamination} The reference $\bar\mu^{(-k)}$ includes the adjacent years $l = k \pm 1$, whose circulations retain dependence on $\tilde Z_k$ through ocean memory — failure mode 1 of @sec-ident. If such residual alignment exists it moves the reference toward the aligned cell and changes $\Theta_k$. The effect is well inside the noise in both boxes, and in Box A the $10.8\%$ is on a small number. # Caveats and concerns {#sec-caveats} ## The identification did not disappear; it moved into the estimand $\widehat\Theta_k$ is unbiased for $\Theta_k$ **unconditionally** — that part of the claim is exactly true, and it is a genuine improvement over identifying a target only under an assumption. But @eq-bridge shows the price: $\Theta_k = \Pi_k$ requires (P$'$), and the honest summary is that **(P$'$) has been demoted from an identification condition to an interpretation condition.** Under the companion report's framing, if (P) fails there is no well-defined target and $T_k$ estimates nothing in particular. Under this one, $\widehat\Theta_k$ still estimates $\Theta_k$ exactly; what fails is only the claim that $\Theta_k$ *is* preferential sampling, and @eq-cmatrix says precisely what it is instead. That separation is real and useful — the estimate and its standard error survive independently of the interpretive assumption, which is what makes reporting them defensible even where the permutation test's assumptions are rejected. It is not the same as needing no assumption at all, and this report should not be cited as though it were. Two further points from @sec-ident belong in any summary of the result. The reference floor $s_k/\sqrt{M-1}$ is not in @tbl-theta's standard errors and is about two-thirds of them; and it is itself a superpopulation quantity, so quoting it requires an exchangeability assumption over circulations that nothing else in the report needs. $\mu^\star$ is not identifiable from these data, so the floor sizes the gap and cannot correct it. ## The conservativeness claim is an assumption, not a theorem It is tempting to argue that any residual memory in the reference must *attenuate* $\Theta_k$, so that the estimand is conservative and the true preferential bias is larger. @sec-ident's second point shows the argument is signed: it presumes the off-diagonal $c_{lk}$ carry the same sign as the diagonal. A lag-$1$ flow could as easily be anti-aligned with $\tilde Z_k$, in which case the reference is deflated and $\Theta_k$ is *inflated*. In these data the measured direction is the inflating one, weakly and insignificantly (@sec-contamination). So "conservative" should be recorded as an assumption about the sign of ocean memory that these ten years do not support, rather than as a property of the estimand. The defensible statement is two-sided: the reference may be contaminated in either direction, the measured contamination is consistent with zero, and dropping adjacent years moves the pooled estimate by less than $2\%$ where it is large. ## What $\Theta_k$ cannot separate - **Mechanism.** $\Theta_k$ cannot distinguish floats accumulating where the water is warm from floats and heat being redistributed together by the same eddies. Both satisfy $[S,X] \ne [S][X]$ in the sense of @diggle2010, and no design-based contrast will split them; that needs a model-based lens. - **A persistent preferential bias.** By @sec-ident's first point, coupling that is common to all $M$ flow years is absorbed into the reference and reads as zero. The construction measures only the component of the coupling that varies within the record, and reclassifies the perfectly persistent component as coverage bias — defensibly, since that component *is* removable by reweighting, but the reader should not read $\Theta_k \approx 0$ as "no preferential sampling". - **One realisation per year.** $\Pi_k$ is a single draw of the flow--field coupling. The ten analysis years are the replication, which is why the pooled row and the drift are the defensible statements and no individual year is. Doubling $D$ shrinks the Monte Carlo error but touches neither the between-year spread nor the reference floor, and @tbl-pooled and @tbl-refnoise show both are comparable to it. - **Two boxes.** Box B and Box A are matched on seeding law, margin, cadence, and over-density against real Argo, and differ in field amplitude ($3.3\times$), gradient, and current speed simultaneously. The pattern is consistent with the contrast requiring both a structured field and an energetic flow, but two boxes cannot attribute it to either. ## Inherited from the ensembles These carry over unchanged from the companion report and are not repaired by the new framing. - **Simulation, not observation.** GLORYS12 is a reanalysis; $\tilde Z$ is what remains after the fitted mean field $m(\cdot)$ is removed, and inherits whatever that fit left behind. $\Theta_k$ is a property of this simulated system. - **Density.** Both virtual arrays run $2.4$--$2.6\times$ denser than the real Argo record over the same boxes. That leaves $\mathbb{E}[B]$ alone but narrows every sampling distribution, so the Monte-Carlo standard errors here are optimistic relative to a real-density array by roughly $\sqrt{2.5}$. The reference floor is unaffected, since it is a property of the flow ensemble. - **The seeding rectangle is not ocean-masked**, so about $3\%$ of Box B seeds land on land and never move. Those floats never enter $\hat Z$; the effect is a reduction in effective $n$, common to every flow year, and it cancels from $\Theta_k$ by the same argument as coverage bias. - **$n$ is endogenous.** Retentive flow years hold more floats, so $\hat Z$ is a ratio estimator and the cells are matched only conditional on $n$. This is precisely the heteroscedasticity @tbl-var measures. ## Suggested changes to the written method - Section 5 of the method draft bounds the pooled variance by $\max_k \operatorname{Var} (\widehat\Theta_k)$, or proposes estimating it from replicate subsamples. Neither is necessary: the per-draw unit statistic $U^{(l,d)}$ gives the pooled variance in closed form, exactly and with no resampling, and the bound is loose by $3.4$--$3.8\times$ in these data. The same construction yields the full covariance $\Sigma$, without which the drift analysis is not available. - The homoscedastic reduction should be demoted to a remark, since its premise is measurably false. - The decomposition $\mu^{(l)} = \mu^{\circ} + \delta^{(l)}$ must state that the identification reference is the **population** mean footprint $\mu^\star$, not the finite grand mean. As written it is ambiguous, and under the finite reading the identifying condition collapses to $\Theta_k = 0$. - The remark asserting that memory in the reference attenuates $\Theta_k$ should be restated as a signed assumption, with the two-sided version given above. # Numerical audit ::: {#tbl-audit .cell execution_count=10} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=10} ```{=html}
